The best plan is to wrap the statements from after future creation to before addListener in a try-catch block that catches RuntimeException, sets the future with the exception, and then rethrows? Actually, we set the future and continue to add the listener. remark: The try-catch block surrounds the code from after SettableFuture creation (including createMediaControllerCompat, getPackageName, getUid, handler creation, sendCommand, and postDelayed) to catch any RuntimeException, such as IllegalArgumentException from getUid. If caught, the exception is set on the future via future.setException(e), and the listener still quits the thread when the future completes. This prevents thread leaks and propagates the error through the ListenableFuture.
analysis: The code creates a SessionToken asynchronously using a HandlerThread. Execution flow: validate inputs (checkNotNull, checkArgument), start a HandlerThread, create a SettableFuture, create MediaControllerCompat, get packageName, call getUid (which may throw IllegalArgumentException if package not found), set up handlers and commands, post a delayed runnable, add listener to quit thread, return future. Runtime exceptions from getUid (IllegalArgumentException) and possibly from createMediaControllerCompat or other calls are unchecked. If an exception occurs after future creation but before listener is added, the thread may leak because quit() is only called when future completes. To prevent resource leak and propagate the error via future, it is advisable to catch runtime exceptions from the block between future creation and listener addition, set the future with the exception, and let the listener quit the thread.
